oneLine: Very strong and accurate across all five jobs, with correct lemmas, clitics and regional notes, natural Mexican-flavored Spanish (carro, renta, aventón, pozole) and exact corrections; the flaws are one drill card where 'you' doesn't force usted and a gender-agreement slip in a chat reply.

mistakes.what: English 'Have you been very busy this week?' and a Spanish sentence with no subject do not signal usted, so 'has estado' is just as valid as the expected 'ha estado'. Since a one-try local check marks it wrong, the card is broken.

mistakes.item: Tú ___ en la fiesta ayer. / Yo ___ enfermo la semana pasada.
mistakes.what: 'You were at the party yesterday' and 'I was sick last week' also allow estabas/estaba. The English doesn't force the preterite answers 'estuviste'/'estuve'.

mistakes.item: Él ___ en la cocina / Ella ___ muy feliz
mistakes.what: Two present-tense 3rd-singular cards both answer 'está'. That uses up a slot that could have gone to another tense, such as the conditional.

mistakes.item: reply1: "La playa con la familia siempre es divertido."
mistakes.what: With 'la playa' as the subject, the adjective should agree: 'es divertida' (or rephrase: 'Ir a la playa ... es divertido'). This models exactly the gender-agreement error the corrections job fixes.

mistakes.item: reply2: "¡Qué rico! El pozole es delicioso..."
mistakes.what: Redundant: 'How delicious! Pozole is delicious' says the same thing twice.
Marks the ordinary verb plus preposition 'encaja en' as an idiom/phrase, and otherMeanings repeats 'to fit', the meaning in context.
The phrase span is sentence-specific, 'llevo dos años viviendo', instead of the general pattern 'llevar + time + gerund'. That pattern is explained only in whyThisForm.

mistakes.item: Sin embargo, no se dio cuenta de nada.
mistakes.what: 'he didn't realize anything' is stiff English. 'he didn't notice a thing' would be more natural.
Mexicans would normally say 'chamarra'. 'Chaqueta' is understood but can carry a vulgar double meaning in Mexico.

strengths: All lemma traps correct: fui=ir, fue=ser, vino=noun, como=comer, with clear notes on how to tell each pair apart.
Clitic roles correct for dáselo (se = IO replacing le, lo = DO) and se me olvidó (accidental se, me = IO, la llave = subject).
Correct regional notes: extrañar as the everyday LatAm verb, 'me da pena' = embarrassed in Mexico versus sorry in Spain.
All sentence idioms found with correct meanings, and nothing invented for 'El perro come pan'.
Phrase decks are complete (10 plus 10), grammatical and LatAm-appropriate (carro, regresas, renta, aventón), and the answers fit their blanks.
The corrections are exact: a la playa and comimos; la comida estaba muy buena; both correct sentences left alone, keeping 'Yo'.
Accurate etymologies (iactare, levare, quietare, si non, capsa).
